the confirmation gate caught a CRITICAL regression that Panel R itself introduced — exactly why consecutive clean panels are required. opus: Panel R fixed the nested-def body leak by having each of the five `_direct_*` driver loops `continue` on a top-level stmt that is itself a def. But a def's HEADER expressions — decorator calls/arguments (`@registry(make_validator())`) and a nested class's base expressions (`class L(get_base())`) — execute in the ENCLOSING function's scope at definition time, yet were syntactically part of the skipped statement. They aren't recovered elsewhere (`_decorator_edges` edges only the decorator name; `_walk_scope` edges a base only via `_name_of`, None for a Call). So a symbol used only there got zero inbound edges and was flagged dead — pre-R it erred safe (over-attributed to the enclosing fn), post-R it erred UNSAFE (false dead, the cardinal sin). Fixed with `_def_header_refs`: when the driver hits a nested def, it still walks the def's header (decorators + class bases/keywords) in the enclosing scope while skipping the body — restoring the dropped enclosing-scope refs without re-introducing the body leak (verified: outer no longer calls a body-only callee; build now reaches make_validator/make_base; self-scan unchanged at 3 advisory). haiku: clean (FINDINGS: none) after 48 adversarial tests verifying the Panel R fixes, the cardinal invariant across Python/TS/JS, metric-dedup, and cross-language parity. diversity 2/2 (opus+haiku full under the updated rule). Streak resets to 0.

two more instances of the nested-scope class (Panel Q), in the two remaining nesting hosts — both CRITICAL false-deads, both pre-existing (not regressions). haiku: a Python def nested in a CONTROL-FLOW block (`if`/`for`/`while`/`try`/`with`/`match`) was never modeled — `_def_node`/`_walk_scope` walked only a function's *direct* body, so a def in an `if` got no node while `_walk_scope` emitted edges from its qualname (phantom source) -> a symbol used only there flagged dead. opus: the tree-sitter twin one host deeper — a def nested in a JS/TS ARROW function (`const h = () => { function w(){...} }`, pervasive) was never modeled because the arrow-declarator branch created the node but never recursed into the arrow body nor threaded the containment edge. Rather than wait for panels to find hosts one at a time, did a SYSTEMATIC nesting-host audit: a def can nest only in a function body (Q), class body (P), control-flow block, or function-expression/arrow (lambdas/comprehensions can't hold defs). Fixes: Python `_scope_defs` looks *through* control flow (no qual level added) in `_def_node`/`_walk_scope`/`_iter_funcs`/the module loop; tree-sitter arrow branch now recurses into the arrow body + emits the containment edge. Test matrix pins every host in both extractors (148 tests). Dogfood: find_stale still 3 advisory, 0 holes (precision intact). diversity 2/2.
